title: Baikal Airlines 130
summary: Tu-154M experienced engine starter failure in No. 2 engine during startup with an alarming red light indication that warned of dangerous air start unit rotational speed. The flight crew ignored the warning, deemed it a false alarm based on aircraft design knowledge and flight manual guidance stating such alarms do not require immediate action. As thrust was set for takeoff, the starter mechanism rotated at dangerous speed, rupturing oil and hydraulic lines in the engine compartment. This ignited an uncontrollable fire and destroyed the aircraft's hydraulic systems causing loss of control in initial climb. The aircraft crashed into a dairy farm near Irkutsk killing all occupants.
probable_cause: Engine starter failed and broke apart, rupturing oil and hydraulic lines and igniting fire that destroyed the aircraft's hydraulic systems. Crew misidentified the red alarm as false based on design assumptions, inadequate training on alarm significance, and flight manual guidance that did not require immediate action for such alerts.

factors.evidence: No. 2 engine's turbo compressor had spontaneously rotated when it should have required pressing the air bleeding button which they had not
A red alarm light suddenly turned on warning the crew about the dangerous speed of the air start unit on engine two
crews deemed it impossible for such a thing to happen so they rejected the warning as a false alarm based on their knowledge of the Tupolev Tu-154 design
the flight manual stated that such an alarm was not a cause for an emergency and would not require immediate action
the engine completely failed and exploded outwards with pieces slicing the fuel and hydraulic lines within the compartment
due to the damaged hydraulic lines the crew could not control the aircraft
First Officer Zhavoronkov told the crew that the aircraft was uncontrollable and it crashed at a speed of 510 km/h

events.text: Engine two failed to start initially and did not respond to restart attempts, finally lighting after nearly 17 minutes with Captain Gennady frustrated at the maintenance crew
A red light warning suddenly turned on indicating the dangerous speed of the air start unit on engine two
Flight engineer Karpov tried to turn off the light but failed and informed the pilots who discussed the problem
After deliberation the crew decided to ignore the alarm altogether knowing they had faced the same problem before
The engine completely failed and exploded outwards with pieces slicing the fuel and hydraulic lines within the compartment igniting in-flight fire
The aircraft became uncontrollable as the hydraulics ran out from fire damage with First Officer Zhavoronkov reporting the aircraft was uncontrollable
The aircraft kept descending and gained speed tremendously before crashing into a dairy farm in village of Mamony 15 km from Irkutsk airport at 510 km/h

specific flight times and crash location confirmed

title: Aeroflot 593
summary: The relief captain brought his teenage children to the cockpit against regulations. While seated at the controls, the 15-year-old son partially disengaged the autopilot's aileron control with a control column input, causing the aircraft to roll into a steep bank approaching 90 degrees. The pilots managed to recover briefly, but the first officer over-corrected during pullup, causing a stall and spin from which they could not recover before descending below safe altitude.
probable_cause: The presence of unauthorized children in the cockpit and the son's inadvertent input to the control column caused partial autopilot disengagement. The pilots' confusion about the aircraft's status, combined with inappropriate recovery inputs and descent below safe recovery altitude, led to the accident.

factors.evidence: Eldar had applied enough force to the control column to contradict the autopilot for 30 seconds, causing the flight computer to switch the plane's ailerons to manual control
The flight path indicator changed to show a 180-degree turn, which the pilots thought indicated a holding pattern, confusing them for nine seconds
The pilots were apparently failed to notice the silent indicator light, having previously flown Soviet-designed planes that had audible warning signals
The first officer over-corrected when pulling up, causing the plane to stall and enter into a spin
The first officer over-corrected when pulling up, causing the plane to stall and enter into a spin
The aircraft crashed into the mountain range after descending beyond safe altitude for recovery

Eldar occupied the pilot's seat as the second child entered the cockpit

title: China Airlines 140
summary: China Airlines Flight 140 stalled and crashed during approach to Nagoya on April 26, 1994, when the first officer inadvertently selected the takeoff/go-around setting while at 1,000 feet altitude. The pilots attempted to correct the situation but failed to disengage the autopilot, which continued to pitch the aircraft up against the pilots' nose-down inputs. The resulting stall killed 264 of the 271 people on board.
probable_cause: Pilot error in failing to disconnect the autopilot after inadvertent TO/GA selection and the TO/GA remaining engaged, combined with the crew's subsequent manual go-around input that increased the nose-up attitude to a point where an aerodynamic stall occurred.

factors.evidence: The aircraft stalled resulting in extreme nose-up attitude with decreasing airspeed due to insufficient thrust.
The first officer inadvertently selected the takeoff/go-around setting at 1000 ft above ground level.
The crew did not disconnect the autopilot, which was still acting on the inadvertent go-around command.
The pilots executed a manual go-around, pulling back on the yoke and adding to the nose-up attitude the autopilot was already executing.
The pilot had been trained for the A300 on a flight simulator in Bangkok which was not programmed with the problematic GO-AROUND behavior.

events.text: Flight took off from Chiang Kai-shek International Airport; descent started at 19:47 and aircraft passed outer marker at 20:12.
First officer inadvertently selected takeoff/go-around setting just 3 nautical miles from runway threshold at 1000 feet AGL.
Pilots attempted to correct manually reducing throttles and pushing yoke forward but autopilot moved horizontal stabilizer to full nose-up position.
Pilots executed manual go-around pulling back on yoke, increasing nose-up attitude to extreme pitch.
Aircraft stalled and struck the ground at severe nose-up attitude.

title: China Northwest Airlines 2303
summary: Flight 2303 took off at 08:13 in rain. Twenty-four seconds after takeoff the crew reported floating and abnormal sound. At 08:16:24 and 08:16:58 the crew reported unstable pitch-up of 20 to 30 degrees. At 08:17:06 unable to maintain altitude, the crew engaged the autopilot which unexpectedly caused a right turn. At 08:22:27 stall warning activated and the aircraft banked left dropping 1833 m in 12 seconds. At 08:22:42 the aircraft disintegrated in-flight. Maintenance had reversed autopilot yaw and bank channels causing violent oscillations that overstressed the airframe.
probable_cause: Autopilot maintenance error where yaw and bank control channels were reversed, causing violent roll oscillations that exceeded structural limits.

factors.evidence: at 08:22:42, the aircraft disintegrated in mid-air above the suburb of Tsuitou Village
autopilot yaw-channel had been erroneously connected to the bank control, and the bank-channel to the yaw controls
at 08:22:27, with the aircraft travelling at 373 km/h, the stall warning activated
aircraft became unable to maintain its assigned altitude

events.text: The aircraft took off from Xi'an Xianyang International Airport at 08:13.
Twenty-four seconds after takeoff, the crew reported that the aircraft was floating and making an abnormal sound.
The crew reported an unstable pitch-up to 20 degrees at 08:16:24 and 30 degrees at 08:16:58.
At 08:17:06, the aircraft became unable to maintain its assigned altitude and the crew engaged the autopilot.
At 08:22:27 with the aircraft travelling at 373 km/h, the stall warning activated.
The aircraft then banked dangerously to the left and dropped from 4717 m to 2884 m in 12 seconds at a speed of 747 km/h.
At 08:22:42, the aircraft disintegrated in mid-air above the suburb of Tsuitou Village.

title: USAir 427
summary: Boeing 737-300 was sequenced behind Delta Air Lines Flight 1083 during approach at 6000 feet altitude at approximately 190 knots. At 19:02:57, the aircraft entered the wake turbulence of the Delta 1083 and immediately experienced three sudden thumps and clicking sounds. The rudder then malfunctioned and hardover in the direction opposite to pilot commands. First Officer Charles Emmett held right rudder pedal pressure but the rudder had reversed hard to the left. The aircraft banked left and entered aerodynamic stall with the stick shaker activating as the wing exceeded its critical angle of attack.
probable_cause: The aircraft's rudder malfunctioned and went hard over in a direction opposite to that commanded by the pilots due to hot hydraulic fluid entering the rudder's dual servo valve causing it to freeze in the opposite position, resulting in aerodynamic stall and loss of control from which the crew could not recover.

factors.evidence: rudder malfunctioned and went hard over in a direction opposite to that commanded by the pilots
stick shaker activated and airplane entered an aerodynamic stall caused by the wing exceeding its critical high angle of attack
aircraft entered an aerodynamic stall from which Captain Peter Germano and First Officer Charles B. Emmet III were unable to recover
First Officer Emmett held right rudder pedal pressure and both pilots pulled back on the yoke to counter the decreasing pitch angle while the rudder had reversed hard to the left

events.text: Aircraft at 6000 feet altitude entered the wake turbulence of Delta 1083 which was 4.1 miles ahead
Three sudden thumps, clicking sounds and a louder thump occurred as the 737 began to bank and roll to the left
The autopilot disconnected and First Officer Emmett stomped on the right rudder pedal and held it there unaware that the rudder had reversed hard to the left
The stick shaker activated and the airplane entered an aerodynamic stall as the wing exceeded its critical angle of attack
The aircraft pitched 80 degrees nose-down and banked 60 degrees left while traveling at approximately 300 mph and slammed into a gravel road in a wooded ravine

notes: second longest air crash investigation in NTSB history
rudder servo valve hydraulic fluid freezing confirmed in final NTSB report
